subject: science
passage: The Deosai Plains, a high plateau in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lie under snow for most of the year and are free of it for only about four months. Himalayan brown bears that live there spend the snowy months in hibernation, during which they neither eat nor drink and live entirely on stored body fat. Wildlife biologist Imran Haider fitted several bears with tracking collars and found that during the brief snow-free season they spent nearly all their daylight hours feeding on roots, grasses, and marmots. Haider's observations suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Himalayan brown bears eat more food in a day than bears in warmer regions do.
choices.B: the bears would stop hibernating if food were available on the plateau in winter.
choices.C: marmots make up the largest part of the bears' summer diet.
choices.D: the bears must build up in a few months the reserves that carry them through a much longer fast.

explanation.why: The bears live on body fat alone for about eight snowy months and can feed only during the four snow-free months. Spending nearly all daylight feeding is what you would expect if all the fat for the long fast must be stored in that short window.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not compare these bears' daily intake with that of bears elsewhere.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text does not say what triggers hibernation or whether winter food would change it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text lists roots, grasses, and marmots but does not say which is the largest part of the diet.
explanation.D: Correct. A long fast on stored fat and a short feeding season together explain the near-constant feeding.
